newsitem.title: UK: BP Chemicals joins Indonesia cracker study.
newsitem.headline: BP Chemicals joins Indonesia cracker study.

text.p: BP Chemicals said on Wednesday it has joined a consortium of four Japanese and one Indonesian firms to work on a feasibility study for setting up a new cracker complex in Indonesia.
The naphtha-based cracker would have an initial capacity of 700,000 tonnes of ethylene and 300,000 tonnes of propylene a year.
The plant is being planned at Bojonegoro near Merak on the west coast of Java.

Along with BP Chemicals, the other firms in the consortium are PT Salim Chemicals Corporation of Indonesia, and Sumitomo Corporation, Tomen Corporation, Nichimen Corporation and Mitsui & Co Ltd of Japan.
BP Chemicals said the cracker would supply ethylene by pipeline to PT PENI, Indonesia's first polyethelene plant which came on stream in February 1993.

BP Chemicals owns 51 percent in PT PENI. Mitsui and Sumitomo control 12.5 percent each in the plant with PT Arseto Petrokimia controlling 15 and Sigit Harjojudanto owning nine percent. The polyethylene plant has a current capacity of 250,000 tonnes a year which is being raised to 450,000 by mid-1998 with an option to raise it by another 100,000 tonnes annually.
Apart from PT PENI, two local plants, PT SMI and PT Satomo would also receive ethylene from the new cracker which, depending on the prospects of the study, is expected to go on stream in 2000.
